title: TailSFT: Filtered Fine-Tuning Improves Post-Training Performance
abstract: arXiv:2608.25756v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training drives reasoning and agentic capabilities in modern AI systems, yet a growing body of work shows that it is most effective when used to fine-tune an already capable base model. We question whether existing pipelines yield models that are most suitable for reinforcement learning. Building on prior work highlighting the role of coverage and pass@K as predictors of post-RL performance, we design a simple modification to supervised fine-tuning, TailSFT, which filters out already fit sequences during training, thereby focusing learning on under-modeled regions, or the tail, of the data distribution. We justify and validate the design choices in TailSFT, particularly the specific filtering criteria, through a combination of controlled experiments and theoretical analysis. translated_title: TailSFT：过滤式微调提升后训练性能
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25756v1 公告类型：新 摘要：强化学习后训练推动了现代AI系统中的推理和智能体能力，但越来越多的研究表明，当用于微调一个已具备能力的基座模型时，它最为有效。我们质疑现有流程是否生成了最适合强化学习的模型。基于先前强调覆盖率和pass@K作为后强化学习性能预测因子的工作，我们设计了对监督微调的简单修改，称为TailSFT，它在训练过程中过滤掉已拟合的序列，从而将学习集中在数据分布中未充分建模的区域，即分布的尾部。我们通过受控实验和理论分析相结合的方式，论证并验证了TailSFT中的设计选择，特别是特定的过滤标准。在OLMo-3 7B上，TailSFT通常在数学和编码评估中提升了pass@16性能，绝对提升高达17%，同时几乎不增加额外开销。
tldr: TailSFT通过过滤已拟合序列来聚焦训练于数据分布的尾部区域，从而提升强化学习后训练前的模型能力，在OLMo-3 7B上实现高达17%的绝对性能提升。
en_tdlr: TailSFT improves post-training performance by filtering out already-fit sequences to focus learning on the tail of the data distribution, achieving up to 17% absolute gains on OLMo-3 7B.
